title: Monsters from data
description:
Load monster types from a text file so designers can change them without recompiling.

```
[goblin]
hp = 12
speed = 1.5
loot = coin, dagger
loaded 3 monster types; "slime" missing speed -> default 1.0
```
hints: `<sstream>` gives streams over strings. `std::istringstream in{ text };` reads from a string exactly like `std::cin` (`in >> word >> number`, or `std::getline(in, line)` for one line at a time), and its condition is false once a read fails. `std::ostringstream out; out << "x " << 5; out.str()` builds a string the way `std::cout` prints.
Trim spaces around keys and values; a line starting with `[` starts a new type (lesson 10.08).
Reload the file while the game runs (press a key) to see changes straight away.
requirements: Sections in brackets, `key = value` lines, lists separated by commas.
Unknown keys are reported; missing keys get defaults.
Spawning a monster uses the loaded type by name.
stretch: Let a type inherit from another: `[goblin_chief : goblin]`.
